host.kind: RunPod CPU container (the build pod), Ubuntu 20.04 userland
host.capabilities: CapEff 0x00000000a80405fb: no CAP_NET_ADMIN, CAP_SYS_ADMIN or CAP_NET_RAW
host.why_network_proxy_role: A full OpenShell sandbox needs a Docker, Podman, Kubernetes or MicroVM driver and a network namespace; none is available in this container (see docs/proofof/SANDBOX-V0.md, 2026-09-25). The supervisor's --role network-proxy runs the same OPA policy engine and L7 proxy on a loopback listener without isolation.

openshell.asset_checksum: verified with sha256sum -c against the release's openshell-supervisor-checksums-sha256.txt
openshell.install_size: supervisor binary 32.6 MB; sandbox and prover binaries also fetched (10.8 MB, 32.6 MB) and checksum-verified, not used in the capture

commands: openshell-supervisor --role network-proxy --listen 127.0.0.1:39128 --policy-rules sandbox-policy.rego --policy-data policy.yaml --tls-dir tls --log-level info   (under timeout 60; stderr -> enforcer.log)
not_captured: OCSF JSONL. The network-proxy role has no gateway settings channel, so ocsf_json_enabled stays false; /var/log/openshell-ocsf.2026-09-28.log was created with 0 bytes. The shorthand lines in enforcer.log are the only enforcer record.
Binary identity. The network-proxy role runs with require_binary_identity:false and records the process as -(0). The adapter matches endpoints only for these records and says so in each row.
Whether the proxy opened a TCP or TLS connection to example.net before refusing the GET. The client witness sees the request, not the proxy's upstream socket.
File and syscall attempts. This role runs no sandboxed workload, so there is no Landlock or seccomp layer to observe.

files.policy.yaml: the declared policy used for the capture (ours)
files.enforcer.log: the supervisor's stderr, unedited; byte-identical in content to /var/log/openshell.2026-09-28.log except two millisecond timestamps
files.client-transcript.raw.txt: curl -w output as captured; curl 7.68 left %{url} and %{exitcode} empty, so the lines are not valid JSON
files.proxy-denial-body.json: the proxy's 403 body for example.net, as received
files.witness.jsonl: output of build_witness.py over the transcript and response bodies
